name: Songomby
body:
SONGOMBY
CR 3

This creature’s body resembles a cloven-hoofed ox but has a large hump behind its shoulders. A long neck ends in an equine head, where floppy ears hang over its beady eyes.

XP 800
NE Large magical beast
Init +2; Senses blindsense 10 ft., darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, scent; Perception +10

DEFENSE

AC 15, touch 11, flat-footed 13 (+2 Dex, +4 natural, –1 size)
hp 31 (3d10+15)
Fort +7, Ref +5, Will +2
Weaknesses floppy ears

OFFENSE

Speed 50 ft.
Melee bite +7 (1d8+7)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Special Attacks foul spray

STATISTICS

Str 20, Dex 14, Con 19, Int 7, Wis 12, Cha 7
Base Atk +3; CMB +9; CMD 21 (25 vs. trip)
Feats Combat Reflexes, Run B, Toughness
Skills Perception +10, Survival +2 (+10 when tracking by scent); Racial Modifiers +4 Perception, +8 Survival when tracking by scent

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Floppy Ears (Ex)

A songòmby’s oversized ears often obscure its vision. However, its acute hearing and sensitive sense of smell help compensate for this. When moving at more than half speed, or when in combat, a songòmby treats all other creatures as having concealment from it. Additionally, a songòmby has a 20% chance of being denied its Dexterity bonus to AC against each attack made against it. As a move action, a songòmby can shift its ears aside, removing both these penalties until the start of its next turn.

Foul Spray (Ex)

A songòmby unleashes a blast of bodily fluids at a creature within 30 feet. The songòmby makes either a trip or bull rush combat maneuver (its choice) against the creature, using its Dexterity modifier instead of its Strength modifier for the check (CMB +6). This doesn’t provoke an attack of opportunity. The creature is also exposed to toxic songòmby lant. A songòmby can use this ability up to 5 times per day.

Poison (Ex)

Songòmby Lant—contact; save Fort DC 15, frequency 1/round for 4 rounds; initial effect 2d6 damage; secondary effect 1 Con; cure 1 save. Songòmbys are immune to this poison. The save DC is Constitution-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm hills and plains
Organization solitary, pair, or herd (3–10)
Treasure none

This strange beast is known as the “snake ox,” as its body is in fact that of a white-haired, cloven-hoofed ox with a large hump over its front shoulders and tufts of tawny hair above its hooves and at the tip of its tail. Its neck, however, is even longer than that of a camel and is flexible, enabling it to reach in every direction. Its long, floppy ears give it a whimsical appearance, but its broad lips hide large ratlike incisors that it uses to inflict bloody wounds when its eyes blaze and nostrils flare in a carnivorous fury. Despite its bulky appearance, it is as fast as any horse. It has a cruel demeanor and is patient on the hunt, crouching for hours beneath a tree where its prey may try to take refuge, and spraying them with its foul bodily fluids to try to make them fall down where it can reach them.
